title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON CONSERVATION AND UTILIZATION OF THE MARINE ENVIRONMENT
title_original: 해양환경 보전 및 활용에 관한 법률 시행령
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters mandated by the Act on Conservation and Utilization of the Marine Environment and matters necessary for the enforcement thereof.

Article 2 (Sea area management authority) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall be the sea area management authority having jurisdiction over the following sea areas under subparagraph 8 b of Article 2 of the Act on Conservation and Utilization of the Marine Environment (hereinafter referred to as the "Act"):
  1. Sea areas over which the Republic of Korea has jurisdiction regarding the conservation of the marine environment in accordance with the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea;
  2. Environmental management sea areas under Article 15 of the Marine Environment Management Act;
  3. Sea areas within the following harbors and ports:
  a. State-owned fishery harbors defined in subparagraph 3 a of Article 2 of the Fishing Villages and Fishery Harbors Act;
  b. Trade ports and coastal ports under Article 3 (1) of the Harbor Act.

Article 3 (Establishment of marine health assessment system) (1) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall establish guidelines for marine health assessment, including items of assessment items and indexes, to assess marine health under Article 5 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "marine health assessment").
  (2) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall comply with the guidelines for marine health assessment under paragraph (1) when conducting a marine health assessment.
  (3) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies or the competent Metropolitan City Mayor, Do Governor, or Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter referred to as "Mayor/Do Governor") to submit relevant materials, if necessary for the marine health assessment.
  (4) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall publicly announce the results of the marine health assessment on the relevant website or by other similar means, for the conservation and utilization of the marine environment.

CHAPTER II FORMULATION OF COMPREHENSIVE PLANS FOR MARINE ENVIRONMENT

Article 4 (Formulation of comprehensive plans for marine environment) (1) Where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries intends to formulate a comprehensive plan for the conservation and utilization of the marine environment under Article 10 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "comprehensive plan for the marine environment"), the Minister shall specify annual implementation details and other relevant matters.
  (2) "Modification of minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso of Article 10 (2) of the Act means any of the following:
  1. Changing the costs incurred in implementing the comprehensive plan for the marine environment within a range of 30/100;
  2. Modifying a comprehensive plan for the marine environment due to an amendment to any other statute or regulation or a modification of a plan under such statute or regulation, which does not affect the objectives, directions for implementation, and phased strategies of such comprehensive plan;
  3. Correcting a miscalculation, a clerical error, an omission or any other similar obvious error.
  (3) Upon receipt of a comprehensive plan for the marine environment under Article 12 (1) of the Act, the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and Mayors/Do Governors may formulate and implement an annual action plan for matters under their jurisdiction (hereinafter referred to as "action plan") to implement such comprehensive plan. In such cases, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may request such heads and Mayors/Do Governors to submit the action plan.
  (4) Upon receipt of action plans submitted under the latter part of paragraph (3), the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall compile and analyze the plans and notify the heads of the relevant central administrative agencies and the Mayors/Do Governors of the results thereof.

Article 5 (Establishment of marine environmental standards) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries and Mayors/Do Governors shall establish or modify marine environmental standards under Article 13 (1) of the Act and regional marine environmental standards under paragraph (2) of that Article by the following methods:
  1. The standards shall be classified by the characteristics and intended uses of each sea area;
  2. The standards shall be classified by seawater quality, marine sediments, and marine organisms.

Article 6 (Marine spatial plans) (1) A marine spatial plan under Article 15 (2) of the Act shall include the following:
  1. Policy directions for spatial management of the marine environment;
  2. Characteristics and current status of each marine environmental space;
  3. Matters regarding the demand for the use and development of marine environmental space and its conservation;
  4. Matters regarding the structure and functional allocation, such as management measures by zone or by use for marine environmental space;
  5. Other matters deemed necessary by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries for spatial management of the marine environment.
  (2) If necessary to formulate a marine spatial plan under paragraph (1), the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and Mayors/Do Governors to submit materials.
  (3) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may prepare management guidelines for the systematic management and sustainable use of the marine environment by zone or by use in accordance with the formulated marine spatial plan.

Article 7 (Response to marine climate change) (1) "Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as surveys on the sea, impact prediction, and adaptation" in Article 17 (1) of the Act means the following:
  1. Matters regarding surveys on the impact of climate change on the marine environment and the prediction of such impact;
  2. Matters regarding climate change adaptation measures, including expansion of carbon sinks in the marine and fisheries sector;
  3. Matters regarding reduction of greenhouse gas emissions through the use of marine areas;
  4. Other matters deemed necessary by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries to respond to climate change.
  (2) If necessary to prepare policies necessary for the matters specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, Mayors/Do Governors, or the heads of relevant institutions or organizations to submit materials.

Article 8 (Comprehensive marine environmental surveys) (1) The subjects of a comprehensive marine environmental survey under Article 18 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "comprehensive marine environmental survey") shall be as follows:
  1. The status of the marine environment, including seawater quality, marine sediments, and marine organisms;
  2. The causes of marine pollution;
  3. Other matters deemed necessary to survey regarding the current status and changes of the marine environment, as determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
  (2) If a Mayor/Do Governor intends to conduct a marine environmental survey of a sea area under his or her jurisdiction under Article 18 (2) of the Act, the Mayor/Do Governor shall report a survey plan, including survey items and timing, to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries before conducting the survey.
  (3) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may provide technical and administrative support for a marine environmental survey under paragraph (2).

Article 9 (Marine environmental quality assessment) (1) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall establish criteria for marine environmental quality assessment under Article 19 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "marine environmental quality assessment") by classifying the criteria according to the following:
  1. Seawater quality;
  2. Marine sediments;
  3. Marine organisms.
  (2) If the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries conducts a marine environmental quality assessment, the Minister shall utilize the results of a comprehensive marine environmental survey.
  (3) "Marine and fisheries-related plans prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 19 (3) of the Act means those specified in Appendix 1.

CHAPTER III ESTABLISHMENT OF FOUNDATION FOR MARINE ENVIRONMENTAL POLICIES

Article 10 (Integrated marine environmental information network) Marine environmental information to be included in the integrated marine environmental information network under Article 21 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "integrated marine environmental information network") shall be as specified in Appendix 2.

Article 11 (International cooperation projects related to marine environment) (1) "Projects prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as joint surveys of the marine environment and the development of science and technology related to the marine environment" in the former part of Article 24 (2) of the Act means the following projects related to the conservation and utilization of the marine environment:
  1. Joint survey projects on the marine environment;
  2. Projects for the development of science and technology related to the marine environment;
  3. Projects necessary for the domestic implementation of international conventions;
  4. Projects related to international exchange of experts and information, and international conferences;
  5. Other projects deemed necessary by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries for international cooperation.
  (2) Research institutes or academic institutions that may jointly participate in the projects specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) in accordance with the latter part of Article 24 (2) of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on Apr. 30, 2018; Jun. 11, 2019>
  1. Schools under Article 2 of the Higher Education Act;
  2. Research institutes under the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Research Institutes or the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Science and Technology Research Institutes;
  3. Specific research institutes under Article 2 of the Specific Research Institutes Support Act;
  4. The Korea Maritime Transportation Safety Authority established under the Korea Maritime Transportation Safety Authority Act and classification societies under Article 60 (2) of the Ship Safety Act;
  5. The Korea Marine Environment Corporation under Article 96 of the Marine Environment Management Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Corporation");
  6. The Marine Environment Preservation Association established under Article 26 of the Act;
  7. Other national or public research institutes and institutions or organizations designated and publicly notified by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
  (3) An institution that jointly participates in a project specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) and intends to receive support under the latter part of Article 24 (2) of the Act shall submit a project plan to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
  (4) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may, within the budget, subsidize an institution that has filed an application for support under paragraph (3) to cover the expenses incurred in conducting a project specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1).
  (5) An institution that has received support under paragraph (4) shall, upon completion of the relevant project, take measures to ensure that information related to research and surveys on the marine environment under the project is utilized for the establishment of the integrated marine environmental information network.

CHAPTER IV SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 12 (Marine Environment Preservation Association) (1) The Marine Environment Preservation Association (hereinafter referred to as the "Association") under Article 26 (1) of the Act shall have a secretariat and specialized committees.
  (2) The Association may establish a branch in an area where one is needed.
  (3) The Association shall prepare a business operation plan and a draft budget each year and submit them to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries before the commencement of the relevant fiscal year; and if the Association intends to modify any important matters determined by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries among matters in the plan or budget, it shall report the details of such modification and the reasons therefor to the Minister in advance.
  (4) The Association shall prepare a business performance report and a report on the settlement of accounts and submit them to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries within 2 months after the end of the relevant fiscal year.

Article 13 (Entrustment of tasks) (1) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall entrust the following tasks to the Corporation under Article 28 (2) of the Act:?<Amended on Feb. 8, 2022>
  1. Tasks necessary for technical and administrative support for activities to respond to marine climate change by local governments and other relevant entities under Article 17 (2) of the Act;
  2. Comprehensive marine environmental surveys under Article 18 (1) of the Act.
  (2) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may entrust the following tasks to the Korea Maritime Institute established under the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Research Institutes, the Corporation, or the Korea Institute of Ocean Science and Technology under Article 2 of the Korea Institute of Ocean Science and Technology Act, in accordance with Article 28 (2) of the Act:
  1. Tasks regarding marine health assessments under Article 5 of the Act;
  2. Tasks regarding marine environmental quality assessments under Article 19 of the Act.
  (3) When the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries entrusts tasks under paragraph (2), the Minister shall publicly announce the name of the entrusted institutions, the details of entrusted tasks, and other relevant information on the website.
